design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER - task 1 (electric_service_billing_and_trouble, category service). Round 2 (rework after the policy-task audit) - every figure below is the round-2 recomputation.
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 1 printed {"task": 1, "key": "env_0043_rural_electric_cooperative/electric_service_billing_and_trouble/1", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [4, 6, 5]}. Allocation: seasonal minimum settlement 4 factors, seasonal restore fee 6, restore payment 5.
[Why a good test] A new-pivot irrigation member asks only to have his idle Schedule IR pivot restored today and what to pay. The scored numbers are the restore payment he keys in himself (687.68) and the restore fee (145.00). The restore fee's own rule says no restore happens until a payment covering the restore payment stands on the account; the restore payment's rule says it is fixed only after the closed season's annual minimum adjustment line stands on the account; that line is missing, so the agent must bill the seasonal minimum (1512.57) - four factors over the season's lines, the transformer, the peak demand and the member's line-extension project - then compute the payment, then restore.
[Scope snapshot] Task 0 holds the late charge, meter refund, reconnection payment and reconnect fee with their four tools. Claimed here (disjoint): service_ext_seasonal_minimum_settlement, service_ext_restore_payment, service_ext_seasonal_restore_fee; tools bill_seasonal_minimum_25412e46, pay_restore_balance_91f3e2ab (owner=user), restore_seasonal_service_78495a78. Every extended policy is claimed exactly once.
[Problem-tree card] Root service_ext_seasonal_restore_fee. Edge S->Y: state_gate (gate service_payments.amount - the payment column the waited-on row carries; the restore has no base eligibility gate, service_evt_seasonal_idle has none), form state, negated sentence 'No idle account is re-energized, and no restore fee is billed, until the account shows a payment posted on the restore day that covers the restore payment it requires.' resolved_by pay_restore_balance_91f3e2ab (owner user). Edge Y->Z: value_input, gate minimum_line, form state, affirmative 'The restore payment is fixed only after the account carries the annual minimum adjustment line its closed season owes, dated after the account went idle.' resolved_by bill_seasonal_minimum_25412e46. One value_input edge >= max(2-1,1). Chain Z, Y, S. Four-point test passes on both. Annual minimum adjustment lines are booked only by the seasonal minimum tool. Correction (audit G8): two user tools post a phone card payment row - this task's pay_restore_balance_91f3e2ab and task 0's pay_reconnection_amount_66e1876e - so the waited-on payment state is not single-write at the row level; the hop is fixed by the business term ('the restore payment', defined only by service_ext_restore_payment) and by the round-2 docstrings, which restrict the two tools to mutually exclusive account states ('your idle seasonal or irrigation service account ... not the line for an account disconnected for nonpayment' versus 'your electric service account that stands disconnected for nonpayment ... not the line for an idle seasonal or irrigation account'); this account is idle, so exactly one tool fits.
[Unmet at the opening] Y->Z: idle_date 2025-11-24, last usage lines dated 2025-11-22, no adjustment line. S->Y: latest payment 2026-04-03 (80.00), none on 2026-04-07, status idle.
[Deletion sensitivity, actual run] skip Z -> restore payment 183.54 instead of 687.68; skip Y -> terminal balance 1730.06 instead of 1042.38 and no payment row. No user hint: the persona names no minimum or adjustment; only the passive 'If the representative tells you something has to be billed or settled on the account before they can give you the figure, you tell them to go ahead'. Tools do not block: the payment and restore bodies read only the account row and write.
[Factor card - seasonal minimum, gold 1512.57, whole baseline 1644.56] seasonal_minimum_rate_per_kva (parameter, multi-source, cross-difficulty line): connected 11 months AND Irrigation Well Extension closed -> 25.00; the long-standing tier (round 2: 120 months connected and no late charge in twelve months, replacing the capital-credit conjunct the audit found entailed - G14) is out by both conditions; baseline 22.80 -> 1300.42. seasonal_minimum_capacity_measure (method): peak 52.6 kW below 75 -> 105.2; baseline 150 kVA -> 2539.24. seasonal_minimum_credited_lines (parameter; round-2 ladder after audit G2): demand lines in 1-3 billing periods -> facility + energy; in 4-6 -> facility + energy + half the demand; otherwise (none, or 7+) facility + energy + demand. The June-August pumping season puts three periods on tier 1 -> 898.26 credited; baseline -> 635.39. The PCA tier (universal) and its override of 'Power cost adjustment, sales tax and fees never count toward either minimum.' are gone; that base sentence is inherited again. seasonal_minimum_proration (parameter since round 2, G1 plausible): 11/12; baseline 1 -> 1731.74. Guaranteed 25.00 x 105.2 x 11/12 = 2410.83; 2410.83 - 898.26 = 1512.57.
[Factor card - restore payment, gold 687.68, whole baseline 1585.06] minimum_adjustment_hold_back (parameter): 1512.57 >= 300, connected < 36 months -> 1008.43 held; baseline -> 1696.11. facility_charge_prepaid_with_restore (parameter; round 2 replaces the deposit-due factor because the seeded deposit could not arise under the deposit charter - audit T1-1 - and the deposit row is removed): first restore of a new service (connected 11 months, no restore fee on file) -> one facility charge 54.00; baseline -> 633.68. uncleared_payments_added_back (method): echeck 80.00 four days old, no return -> added back; baseline -> 607.68. idle_season_late_charge_hold_back (parameter): 5.00 of 2025-12-13 held (the 7.13 of 2025-09-12 predates the idle - the near-miss); baseline -> 692.68. area_light_lines_while_out (parameter, cross-difficulty light): the light's confirmed light-out of 2026-03-30 (round 2; the old 2026-01-09 date would have owed an outage credit under the light charter, audit T1-2) -> the out month's rental 17.95 held; baseline -> 705.63. 1585.06 - 1008.43 - 5.00 - 17.95 + 80.00 + 54.00 = 687.68.
[Factor card - restore fee, gold 145.00, whole baseline 45.00] restore_charge_by_meter (parameter, multi-source): CT meter AND demand lines -> 110.00; baseline 45.00 -> 80.00. idle_period_inspection (parameter): 4 months -> 20.00; baseline -> 125.00. area_light_visit_on_restore (parameter, cross light): out_of_service -> 15.00; baseline -> 130.00. collection_review_period (method, window convention; new in round 2 - the round-1 restore multiplier was a number substitution, audit G1): a service connected less than twelve months is reviewed over its whole life (12 months counting the month in progress) instead of the months since the idle date; baseline since the idle date (one late charge -> 10.00) -> 125.00. collection_review_on_restore (parameter): two late charges in the period (2025-09-12, 2025-12-13) -> 30.00; baseline -> 115.00. line_extension_warranty_credit (parameter, cross-difficulty line; replaces the deposit addition): extension energized 2025-04-10, 11 months -> 30.00 off; baseline -> 175.00. 110 + 20 + 15 + 30 - 30 = 145.00. The standard review period is now stated in the same whole-month form as compute ('dated less than the whole months elapsed since the idle date before the current date'), closing audit G6.
[Overrides and inheritance] Seasonal minimum: overwrite of service_evt_minimum_bill's December annual-minimum sentence only. Restore fee: overwrite of 'A restore is billed seasonal_restore_fee.'; the back-billing of facility charges for restores before seasonal_idle_min_months stays inherited and does not bite (4 whole months idle, IR minimum 4). Restore payment: no base provision for a payment amount, overwrite [].
[Base-invariant card] account_billable: status idle is billable. cash_only_channel: cash_only_until empty. service_evt_minimum_bill and service_evt_seasonal_idle: policy_scope; the restore rides on the member's confirmed seasonal_restore order of 2026-04-06 (a pre-existing record), IR allows seasonal idles, the account is idle.
[Business-object card] Account 23-4152-017 (meter 41865530). Minimum object: lines dated in the twelve months before 2026-04-07; the connect fee and rental lines are not credited. Restore payment object: the balance after the adjustment, with held-back rows identified by charge_component and date. Restore object: the confirmed seasonal_restore order, completed by the restore.
[Seed rows] customers: Clayton Deering (0418452, 2705551776, 1386). service_accounts: the idle IR pivot (connected 2025-04-14, idle 2025-11-24, balance 72.49 = November bill 75.69 + late 5.00 + December-March rentals 71.80 - echeck 80.00). service_charges: eight season bills (facility, energy, PCA, demand June-August), twelve LED 110W rentals, the connect fee, late charges 7.13 (2025-09-12) and 5.00 (2025-12-13). service_payments: on-time echecks, the late office check, the 80.00 echeck of 2026-04-03. Cross: line project (closed 2025-05-02, energized 2025-04-10), light rental (out_of_service since 2026-03-30, inside the ten business days before an outage credit runs). Service orders: idle completed, restore confirmed. No deposit or capital rows are seeded or read in round 2. Automatic clauses: no notice (past due 80.69 < 150.00), no back-bill, no light outage credit yet.
[Persona] Friendly, rushed farmer; volunteers the goal, the hard preference and the situation; only when asked: credentials, name, location, 'about eighty dollars' paid online, the yard light that quit about a week ago and was called in on the app (round 2, consistent with the confirmed light-out; the round-1 'house meter' mention, which had no record, is removed). Passive reactions only; no ask of his own; no computed answer.
[Reachability] Locate and verify; read account, charges, payments, orders, light, line project; the restore-fee rule sends the agent to the restore payment, whose rule sends it to the adjustment line; bill 1512.57; compute 687.68; hand over the idle-account payment line; he pays; restore with the order id and 145.00. All synchronous at frozen_time 2026-04-07 09:40 CDT.
[Standard solution and traps] Writes: 1512.57, 687.68, 145.00. Traps: billing the minimum on 150 kVA at 22.80 for the full year crediting facility, energy and demand (the whole baseline 1644.56; round 1's dossier misstated it as 1678.44, audit finding 4, corrected); crediting the demand lines; quoting the plain balance 72.49 or 1585.06; forgetting the echeck add-back or the facility prepayment; holding back the September 2025 late charge; reviewing late charges since the idle date only; restoring at the flat 45.00 fee.
[Verification run, round 2] Evaluator (check_compute internals, gold replayed to each handling time): minimum 1512.57 baseline 1644.56 {1300.42, 2539.24, 635.39, 1731.74}; payment 687.68 baseline 1585.06 {1696.11, 633.68, 607.68, 692.68, 705.63}; restore fee 145.00 baseline 45.00 {80.00, 125.00, 130.00, 125.00, 115.00, 175.00}; skip Z -> 183.54; final balance 1042.38.
[Solvability vs GT] Step 9 binds the account for account_billable; step 11 for cash_only_channel; step 13 is policy_scope with the confirmed order cited as pre-existing stage evidence.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the rule prose, docstrings, persona and finder rows alone the agent reaches the same chain and figures; the alternative readings (calendar year versus twelve whole months, which lines are credited, which review period) are pinned by the rule's whole-month windows and ladders.
[Round-2 rework log] G1: proration relabelled parameter; the restore multiplier replaced by the collection_review_period method (fee 90.00 -> 145.00). G2: credited-lines ladder rewritten on demand billing periods. G6: standard review period stated in compute's whole-month form. G8: docstrings scoped; single-write claim corrected. T1-1 / O1-a / G15: deposit row and both deposit factors removed, replaced by the facility prepayment and the line-extension warranty credit (payment 1097.78 -> 687.68). T1-2 / O1-c: light-out moved to 2026-03-30 and the persona now says it was called in. O1-b: 'house meter' removed. O1-d / G14: capital reads removed. Finding 4 and false assertions (a)-(c): corrected in this dossier. Downstream propagated to computations, tracing, prerequisite_closure, solvability_contract and the read nodes (find_deposit_accounts and find_capital_accounts removed, write steps now 9, 11, 13); all per-task gates re-run green.
[Audit observations, round 2] G9: the S->Y gate is the payment column the waited-on row carries, the restore having no base eligibility gate. G17: the capacity measure compares metered kW with transformer kVA at unity power factor, as the cooperative's irrigation minimum states it; the rule names both units. G18: the restore of the CT meter is priced as a crew visit but completed in the billing system at once, the idle->active transition belonging to the agent in the base lifecycle; no real-world wait gates a later write.
user_scenario:
You are Clayton Deering, a row-crop farmer in his late forties on Brushy Fork Road who put in a new center pivot on the north field last spring; Cedar Fork built the line out to the well for it and the pivot meter has been idle since you shut it down for the winter in late November. April has come in dry, you want to pre-water the north field this week, and last night you put in a request on the SmartHub app to have the pivot meter turned back on today. You are calling member services this morning to get it switched on. You are friendly, a little rushed, and you think in round numbers.

You open by saying you put in a request last night to restore the north pivot and you need it turned on today, and you ask what you need to pay to have it switched on. You will pay whatever it takes today with your card, but you do card payments on the cooperative's automated phone line yourself and do not read card numbers out to anybody. You are not asking about anything else - not a payment plan, not your light.

When the representative asks who you are, you give your membership number, 0418452, and the phone number on the account, 2705551776; if they ask your name, it is Clayton Deering. You do not know the account number; it is the north pivot well on Brushy Fork Road. If asked about recent payments, you say you paid something online last Friday, you think about eighty dollars, and that is all you remember. If asked about the yard light at the well house, you say it quit about a week ago, you called it in on the app, and nobody has been out to fix it yet.

If the representative tells you something has to be billed or settled on the account before they can give you the figure, you tell them to go ahead and do it by the book. When they quote you the amount and hand you over to the automated payment line, you run it yourself for that account and exactly the amount quoted, and you read them the confirmation number it gives you. If the figure seems steep you say so once, then you accept what they confirm. When the representative tells you the restore has been done and the meter is coming back on, you thank them and hang up without raising anything further.
